entrypoints.summary: A request for a product page carries a Referer header; the lab directs replacement of that header's original domain with a generated Collaborator domain.

observability.channel: Burp Collaborator DNS and HTTP interaction log
negative_controls: No independently documented negative/control condition is available in the supplied source.
observability.positive_marker: DNS and HTTP interactions initiated by the application appear after polling, potentially after a short asynchronous delay.

preconditions: Access to the training lab and a product-page request that can be intercepted and resent.
Use of Burp Collaborator's default public server, because the lab firewall blocks arbitrary external systems.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: HTTP product-page request with Referer containing a Burp Collaborator-generated domain.
trigger_steps.summary: Visit a product, intercept its request, replace the Referer domain with a generated Collaborator domain, and send the request.

capabilities.concept: server-side fetch to attacker-selected external URL

relation_candidates.dst: server-side fetch to attacker-selected external URL
relation_candidates.rationale: The lab directs replacement of the Referer domain with a Collaborator domain, after which analytics fetches the specified URL.
The documented outcome is application-initiated DNS and HTTP interactions visible through Collaborator polling.
relation_candidates.src: server-side fetch to attacker-selected external URL

relation_candidates.rationale: Constraining the destinations accepted for analytics fetches restores the stated requirement that Referer cannot select an unintended fetch target; no concrete implementation is supplied.
relation_candidates.src: server-side fetch to attacker-selected external URL

impact.affected_asset: The application's server-side outbound-request capability and network boundary.
impact.attacker_capability: Cause the application to make an HTTP request to the public Burp Collaborator server by controlling Referer.
impact.security_effect: Blind server-side request forgery with externally observable outbound DNS and HTTP requests.

causal_trace.summary: The attacker controls the Referer header sent with a product-page request and substitutes a Burp Collaborator-generated domain.
Analytics treats the Referer-specified URL as a fetch target, allowing a request to an unintended external location rather than constraining the destination.
When a product page is loaded, analytics software fetches the URL specified in Referer; the documented workflow causes an HTTP request to the public Collaborator server.
The application initiates out-of-band DNS and HTTP interactions to the attacker-selected Collaborator domain; execution is asynchronous and observable by polling Collaborator.

failure.operation: Server-side analytics fetch of a Referer-specified URL

primary_invariant.statement: A Referer value accepted on a product-page request must not cause analytics to fetch an attacker-selected or otherwise unintended URL.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The documented lab behavior fetches the URL specified in Referer, and replacing its domain with a Collaborator domain produces application-initiated outbound interactions.

quality.review_notes: This is a deliberately vulnerable PortSwigger training lab and a conceptual SSRF source, not a source-code review or remediation patch. The supplied material documents a reproduction workflow and expected out-of-band observable but contains no per-run Collaborator interaction evidence, implementation code, immutable version, or independently documented negative control. The mitigation class states the inverse of the documented destination-control invariant; no concrete patch is evidenced.

remediation.invariant_restored: Analytics does not perform a server-side fetch to an unintended destination selected through Referer.
mitigation_classes: constrain server-side URL-fetch destinations for analytics input

affected_versions_or_commits.value: Observed 2026-07-16; no explicit immutable page version or implementation commit supplied

target.component: Analytics functionality that fetches the URL specified in a product-page Referer header
target.project_or_package: PortSwigger Web Security Academy blind SSRF lab

oracle.expected_negative: No independently documented negative or control condition is supplied.
oracle.expected_positive: After sending a product-page request whose Referer domain is replaced with a generated Collaborator domain, Collaborator polling reports DNS and HTTP interactions initiated by the application; polling may need to be repeated because the server-side operation is asynchronous.
